_: THE EDITORIAL RECORD OF THE PRESS — hand-maintained, unlike
data/library.json, which is measured from the files themselves.
Everything here is a statement about a volume that a person had to
make: what it is for, who it is for, what a reader will find in it,
and which other volume it sits beside. None of it can be derived,
so none of it is generated — but nothing here may state a FIGURE
either. Page counts, file sizes and the number of volumes are
measured into data/library.json by scripts/build-library.mjs and
read from there, so a number on a publication page cannot have been
typed with confidence into this file.
access: 'open'     — anyone may download it, no account, no enrolment.
'enrolled' — the volume is published and named in full, and
the download comes with enrolment.
Every volume below is 'open', and that is a ruling rather than an
oversight. The two Complete Curriculum editions were moved to the
enrolled tier in this pass on the reasoning that they are what
carries Levels II to VI — and tests/library.test.mjs stopped the
build: the Library page promises in both editions that nothing
published is withdrawn, and a build does not get to overrule that.
Withdrawing a book a reader could download yesterday is the
owner's decision. The tier itself is built, shown and tested, and
it binds the per-level teaching volumes for Levels II to VI as the
Press produces them — which is what the Library has said all along.
A volume is listed here only if the Press has produced it. There is
no entry for a book that would be nice to have, and a locked entry
is not a way to imply one exists — every row below names a file
that is on disk and whose extent is measured.
